title: Deployment Pipelines and Promotion
summary: Combine Git with Fabric deployment pipelines to promote lakehouses, notebooks, warehouses, semantic models and reports from DEV to TST to PRD, with pairing, autobinding, rules and a safe layer order.
audience: Platform architects, data engineers, release managers

pages.title: Overview
pages.description: What the hybrid Git plus deployment pipeline pattern solves, when to use it, and a map of the playbook.

pages.title: Deployment strategy
pages.description: The hybrid pattern, an honest comparison with Git-only and code-first promotion, operating rules and anti-patterns.

pages.title: Pipeline setup and pairing
pages.description: Create a pipeline, assign workspaces, choose the UI, understand item pairing and resolve common setup problems.

pages.title: The manual deployment
pages.description: Compare stages, choose full, selective or backward deployment, deploy with a note, review changes and know what is copied.

pages.title: Autobinding
pages.description: How dependent items stay connected across stages, what binds and what does not, and how to override it.

pages.title: Deployment order and layers
pages.description: One pipeline per medallion layer, the dependency order from Bronze to Delivery, and the deploy, hydrate, verify loop.

pages.title: Supported items and rules
pages.description: The support matrix for Git and pipelines, rule types per item, and worked scenarios for notebooks and semantic models including Direct Lake.

pages.title: Automation and limits
pages.description: Deploy from CI with the REST API, code-first alternatives, workarounds for unsupported items, and permissions.

pages.title: Appendix: IDs and rule values
pages.description: An inventory notebook, queries that return rule values, and a per-stage rule settings template.
